brief: The plaza's paving is the largest uniform surface in the town and it does not age. Give it a per-cell rule: moss and grass creep into the joints between the setts where nobody walks, thickening through wet seasons and dying back in frost and drought, and worn away where feet actually go. The courtyard already has this idea in `trod[]`/`wear[]` and litter, and the plaza has `pavingAt(x,y)` as its one paving predicate - this is that idea, on the other room, as a CA. New CA has four entries in 99 iterations and none of them are here; it is the town's signature kind and the plaza is its emptiest cell.
measured: Grepped on HEAD: `moss`, `weed` and `lichen` appear nowhere in courtyard.html. `trod[]` and `litter[]` are courtyard-only. Nothing greens paving anywhere in the town.
successLooksLike: Two shots of the plaza a season apart, warped from the same start, show visibly more green in the joints after a wet autumn than at the end of a dry summer, and the roundel's walked rings and the bench approaches stay clean. `tileKinds` or the census's green count moves.
avoid: Per-cell variance at the grain the region is addressed by - a scalar that can reach zero needs `hash(x, y+k) > c`, not a global multiply, or the whole plaza flickers as one. It is cached ground: set the dirty flag on the cadence the growth actually changes, not per frame (`ground-rebuilds.mjs`). Do not make it walkable-different: nobody's route changes.
